sentences.text: A dolphin never fully falls asleep. Half of its brain stays awake all night. So who keeps watch?
Dolphins sleep with only one half of their brain at a time, while the other half stays alert.
That is why one eye stays open while they rest, the eye on the awake side. The other one is shut.
They need this because every breath is a conscious choice. A fully sleeping dolphin would stop breathing.
So they rest near the surface, drifting or swimming slowly, rising for air without properly waking up.
The awake half also watches for predators. After a while, the two halves switch shifts.
So if you could nap with half your brain awake, what would your other half be doing? Tell me in the comments.
